what_it_does: The attention mechanism is the core of Transformer AI models: it computes how much each word (or token) in a sequence should "attend to" every other token, which requires a large number of matrix multiplications. Hardware accelerators for attention often use a systolic array — a grid of small multiplier units arranged so that data flows from one unit to the next like water through pipes, enabling high-throughput matrix math. This paper identifies two problems with conventional systolic array designs for attention: the grid shape leads to poor reuse of data (data is loaded but not used enough times before it must be replaced), and running one full attention layer before starting the next causes frequent expensive writes of intermediate results to on-chip fast storage (SRAM — fast, small memory built directly on the chip). The authors redesign the array layout into a "Balanced Systolic Array" that reaches 99.5% hardware utilization (the compute units are doing useful work nearly all the time), and pair it with a scheduling strategy that interleaves multiple rows of the attention computation to reduce intermediate SRAM writes by about 32%.
